tldr: On the fixed disk and straight boundary specialization \(\mathcal M\), exact radius plus a public angular-sector label yields minimax absolute risk and finite-sample ninety-percent honest expected interval length of order \(\max\{n^{-1/3},n^{-1/4}J^{-3/4},(nJ)^{-2/7}\}\). The transitions are \(J\asymp n^{1/13}\) and \(J\asymp n^{1/6}\), without a logarithmic factor. Released-data gradient learning and selected-sector offset regression attain these orders. Every compatible causal supermodel containing this specialization inherits all three lower obstructions and both transitions of the necessary lower envelope. Matching upper bounds and the sufficient resolution threshold are proved on the fixed geometry. There the separately established full-coordinate order is \(n^{-1/3}\), matched precisely when \(\liminf J_n/n^{1/6}>0\).
gap: Distance-based boundary theory and location-based boundary theory concern different observation experiments. They do not state the whole-class angular-resolution surface for exact radius plus a supplied sector label. A generic coordinate-quantization remainder omits unusually informative stationary-direction sectors.
